Check output before release

inspect.Rd

The final inspection before anything leaves the secure environment. inspect() reads every file in output_dir, runs the relevant checks and gives each file one verdict for the person who approves the release:

Usage

inspect(output_dir, config = NULL, real_data = NULL, register = NULL)

Arguments

output_dir

Directory with the output, normally from real_run().

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

real_data

Optional real data (a data frame or a named list of data frames) for the checks that need microdata.

register

Optional directory with the register of earlier releases kept by record_release(). A directory that does not exist yet holds no releases.

Value

An object of class mimic_inspection: files, a data frame with one row per file (file, type, verdict, reasons, description), checks, the full checks per file, and tables, the tables read from the files. It holds output that is not yet approved and stays in the secure environment. Write it for the approver with write_report().

Details

  • APPROVED: every check passed.

  • NEEDS CHANGES: a rule is broken; the reasons say which and where.

  • REVIEW BY HAND: the file could not be checked automatically (images, spreadsheets, unknown objects) or something needs a human judgement. When in doubt, mimic does not approve.

What is checked

  • Tables (.csv, .tsv, data frames in .rds/.RData):

    • cells below min_count with check_min_count(): a count column named n, count, freq or similar, or a cross table whose numeric cells are all whole numbers,

    • minimum, maximum and range values with check_extremes(),

    • tables of magnitudes (sums, means, medians) without a count column are sent for review by hand, because the cell sizes behind them are unknown,

    • row-level data: identifier columns, rows that repeat a combination of the grouping columns (an aggregated table has one row per combination), or (with real_data) many rows or identifier values from the real data.

    • suppressed cells (NA, "<5", ".", ...) that can be recovered from totals in the table with check_suppression(),

    • groups whose persons all share one value with check_group_disclosure(),

    • rows with a suppressed count that still show a share, sum, count of part of the group or other number (n = "<5" next to pct = 0.15 or n_female = 2),

    • counts of part of the group (n_female next to n) checked for small cells like the count, and a suppressed one that is the count minus the other parts (n_female = "<5" next to n and n_male),

    • tables with neither counts nor numbers (a list of dates, places or notes) are sent for review by hand: they list values rather than aggregate them,

  • Models in .rds/.RData with check_model().

  • Pairs of tables with check_differencing(), when they have the same grouping columns or one grouping is part of the other (the finer table is summed up; rows labelled "Total" are left out).

  • Text (the run log, .txt, .md, .html): with real_data, searched for values that could point to a person.

Descriptions

When the researcher described the files with describe_output(), inspect()

  • checks a table by the count and grouping columns named there instead of guessing them, and sends it back when a named column is missing,

  • checks the numbers behind a figure, and sends the figure back when they need changes or are missing (the figure itself is still reviewed by hand),

  • checks the description file like other text, because the researcher wrote it,

  • shows the descriptions in write_report().

With require_description = TRUE in mimic_config(), every output file without a description is sent back.

A table of model coefficients is approved when it carries df_residual (and observations) at or above the limits, as tables from safe_model() do; otherwise it is reviewed by hand.

With the real data

Some rules can only be checked against the microdata. Give real_data and inspect() also

  • applies the dominance rules with check_dominance() to tables of sums and means: a column such as mean_income or sum_income is matched to the variable income, and the table's grouping columns to the variables of the same name,

  • flags numbers in tables that equal a value held by fewer than min_count persons (often a median or extreme of a small group),

  • searches text files, the text cells of tables and file names for identifiers, free text and rare values (a day-precise date, a code or a settlement held by fewer than min_count persons).

Persons are found through identifier columns in the real data: names like person_id, cpr... or pnr..., and the id_vars of the configuration. Add a key with another name (lbnr) to id_vars, or rare values are counted in rows.

Counts are taken as persons

A count column is read as a number of persons, because that is what min_count is about. A table of contacts per settlement can pass with 12 contacts that all belong to one person. Without the real data inspect() cannot tell; with real_data a label held by fewer than min_count persons is found whatever the count next to it says. Ask for counts of persons, not of rows, when the script works on a linked table.

Earlier releases

The most realistic differencing attack does not use two tables from one run but two runs: the same table for all persons, and a month later for all persons except one settlement. Each run has its own empty output directory, so inspect() only sees it with a register. Record what is released with record_release() and give the same register every time: each table is then also compared with every table released before.

Examples

out <- file.path(tempdir(), "inspect_example")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
tab <- as.data.frame(table(settlement = fake_persons$settlement))
names(tab)[2] <- "n"
write.csv(tab, file.path(out, "by_settlement.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(sex = c("F", "M"), n = c(985, 1015)),
          file.path(out, "by_sex.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
res <- inspect(out, real_data = list(persons = fake_persons))
res
#> <mimic_inspection> 2 files in
#> C:/Users/danie/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpCclG4q/inspect_example
#> ℹ No register: tables were not compared with earlier releases.
#> ✖ NEEDS CHANGES: by_settlement.csv
#> • 5 of 22 cells have fewer than 5 persons.
#> • Contains 5 value(s) that could point to a person (free text, or a date, code
#> or label held by fewer than 5 persons).
#> ✔ APPROVED: by_sex.csv
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1 approved, 1 needs changes, 0 to review by hand.
